For the positive trine family, the same construction with Eλ j still gives d ≤4 and the rank argument gives d ≥3. The following sections prove dimension four on a low-noise interval and dimension three on a high-noise interval; the intervening boundary remains unresolved. For m = 3 the unrestricted comparison is exactly four quantum dimensions versus exactly nine classical HMM states. For larger m, marginalizing H over b, d gives T/m. Nonnegative rank cannot increase under this operation, so every finite classical HMM needs at least max{9, rm} states, whereas the quantum minimum remains four. Thus a resolution-dependent classical lower bound survives the broader interface, although it is weaker than the sector bound. No exact classical optimum for m > 3 is claimed.
